newsitem.title: CHINA: China actively buying soybeans, meal on price dips.
newsitem.headline: China actively buying soybeans, meal on price dips.

text.p: China has swept into the world market, buying at least 200,000 tonnes each of soybeans and soymeal for July to September shipment, traders said on Tuesday.
Mixed origin U.S. and South American beans had been purchased in the low $320s inclusive of cost and freight (C&F) to Chinese ports, trading sources said.
Meal was priced at $290-295 per tonne C&F, they said.
The sales were made overnight Monday and on Tuesday, they said.
A strong weather-related sell-off in Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soybean futures resulted in meal prices ending at their lowest level in three months, with July down $8.80 a tonne at $264.80.
With prices at current levels, more Chinese buying could be expected, Asian traders said.
With a crushing margin of around $30 a tonne, China had no need to await further price falls, said a source based in Singapore who completed some of the business.
"Oil prices from South America have not dropped, even though they have in Chicago," he said. "So it makes sense to buy beans."
Trading sources throughout the region said prices were expected to soften further, which might lead to more Chinese buying.
"The most important thing is the margin -- when there is a margin, they move, and now there is a margin," the Singapore trader said.
While the reported buying was based on genuine need, current price levels or anything lower might attract Chinese speculators and lead to future defaults, he said.
This scenario was keeping one major trading house out of the Chinese market, a source who experienced defaults in 1996 said.
He sold one cargo of 10,000 tonnes of low protein soymeal on Tuesday for early September shipment at $293-294 C&F. Origin was optional Brazil or Argentina, he said.
He and others were sceptical of the high sales figures being reported.
But the traders involved said the deals brought China's total soybean purchases on the world market so far in 1996 to more than two million tonnes.
Total soybean imports already stand at 1.5 million tonnes, and with the addition of Tuesday's sales could push through 1.7 million.
